_comment: fleet-telemetry server config for AFIRMICO Auto (SDD-010 section 10.4).
Config deltas from the Tesla reference defaults are deliberate, not cosmetic:
- tls.ca_file is UNSET: the binary already embeds Tesla's production vehicle CA.
Setting it APPENDS to the trust pool, needlessly widening trust.
- records.V is the only record type carrying vehicle data. alerts/errors/
connectivity go to the same logger so 'vehicle asleep' is distinguishable
from 'vehicle broken'.
- transmit_decoded_records true emits JSON, so the forwarder needs no protobuf.
- json_log_enable true is REQUIRED: the forwarder parses JSONL, not text.
- logger.verbose true is REQUIRED. It sets includeTypes in the transformer,
which wraps each value with its type ({doubleValue: 10}). With verbose=false
an invalid signal is emitted as the STRING "<invalid>", which Tier 1 would
store as valid text -- a declined signal silently becoming a measurement.
- log_level info (NOT warn) is REQUIRED, and this is the one setting that
silently destroys telemetry. The logger dispatcher emits every vehicle
payload as an INFO-level record_payload line. At warn, fleet-telemetry
still receives the signals and Tesla still bills for them, but nothing is
written that the forwarder can read -- so the relay ships zero batches and
every downstream table stays empty while Tesla's dashboard shows usage.
Observed: 3 days of live traffic, 84 billed signals, 0 rows forwarded, and
only ONE record_payload line ever written (the synthetic deploy self-test).
At info the log grows with traffic; rotate it (see max-size/max-file) rather
than raising the level back, because raising it does not slow the log --
it stops the data.
